title: de-risking-deployments-half-day-customer-lab-agenda
body:
Purpose:
Run a focused half-day lab (3.5 hours) with customer engineering and product stakeholders to: confirm deployment constraints, validate a minimal integration path for Redwood inference, produce a risk register and next-step plan, and collect quantitative latency/cost baselines for their key flow.

Context / why this exists (notes to self):
- Many customers stall at architecture questions (networking, latency SLOs, model variants, caching).
- We want to make tradeoffs concrete with live measurements and a small integration exercise.
- Keep it pragmatic: leave with a clear go/no-go decision and an action list mapped to owners.

Prework (ask customer 7 days before):
- Provide a short topology diagram (VPC, NAT, subnets, on-prem gateways).
- Identify 2 sample API calls (happy path & large context path) + expected QPS.
- IAM contact + VPN/VPC peering point of contact.
- Install small test harness: curl / python snippet (we can offer a script).

Logistics:
- Duration: 3.5 hours (recommended split below)
- Attendees: customer eng lead, product manager, infra/network lead, security contact (optional), Redwood SE (facilitator), Redwood infra engineer (measurement lead), solutions PM (scribe)
- Location: customer office / remote via Zoom + breakout rooms for hands-on (we'll use persistent Zoom + Miro)
- Equipment: customer laptop with repo access, VPN credentials for test environment, GPU instance (if private test), network capture tool (tcpdump or wireshark)

Agenda (times are flexible):
- 0:00–0:15 — Kickoff (align goals & success criteria)
  - Intro + why we ran this lab (1–2 slides)
  - Confirm success criteria (customer says OK to measurable baseline + plan)
  - Quick roles & parking-lot explanation
- 0:15–0:45 — Topology walkthrough & constraints mapping (customer leads)
  - Collect hard constraints (data residency, firewall rules, approved egress IPs, compliance windows)
  - Flag any blockers for private deployment (air-gap, HSM, no external traffic)
- 0:45–1:15 — Integration approach options (present)
  - Option A: Hosted API with VPC egress + private routing (fastest)
  - Option B: Dedicated capacity with reserved GPU pool (predictable throughput)
  - Option C: Private on-prem deployment (full control, longer lead)
  - For each: tradeoffs (latency, cost, time-to-prod, operational burden)
- 1:15–1:45 — Hands-on: quick-run baseline (happy path)
  - Measurement lead runs the provided harness against customer sample call
  - Capture p50/p95 latency, token throughput, error rates, egress bandwidth
- 1:45–2:00 — Break / notes synthesis (SE and scribe prep short summary)
- 2:00–2:30 — Deeper path: large context / edge-case run
  - Run the long-sequence prompts, emulate cache miss vs cache hit
  - Measure delta in latency & token cost
- 2:30–3:00 — Risk register & mitigations (interactive)
  - Build a table of top 8 risks with owner, mitigation, and impact (High/Med/Low)
  - Typical risks: private network egress, model quality mismatch, request burst handling, monitoring blind spots
- 3:00–3:20 — Decision canvas and recommended next steps
  - Present recommended path + estimated timeline and effort (scoped tasks)
  - Customer to indicate preferred path / outstanding info required
- 3:20–3:30 — Close and immediate action items
  - Capture owners and dates, schedule follow-up 1:1 to unblock infra items

Slide outline (skeleton for presenter slides):
- Title slide: De-risking Deployment Lab — <Customer> (date)
- Goals + success criteria (one slide, with 2 measurable criteria)
- Attendees & roles (one slide)
- Current topology & constraints (diagram)
- Candidate deployment options (one slide with 3 boxes)
- Measurement plan (what we'll run + metrics)
- Live baseline: happy path results (chart + numbers)
- Live baseline: long context results (chart + numbers)
- Cost/latency tradeoff summary (table)
- Risk register (top 8 rows)
- Recommended plan (phases + rough dates)
- Action items & owners (one slide)

Facilitation notes (scripts, tips, and subtle prompts):
- Kickoff: "If we get to the end and you have one clear path and 3 owners assigned, this session is a success."
- When topology discussion stalls: ask "What happens during a failure at 3am? Who gets paged?"
- Keep the tests simple — avoid changing parameters during measurement window unless clearly labeled in notes.
- If security contact pushes for a full audit: capture it as a follow-up item; don't let it derail the lab.
- Use a red/yellow/green confidence quick poll after each measurement block (one-slide poll screen share).
- Parking lot examples: legal review timeline, procurement lead time, certs needed for on-prem nodes.

Measurement & capture (how we record):
- Scribe: record p50/p95, tokens consumed, CPU/GPU utilization, error codes, egress bytes per minute, test parameters
- Save logs to shared folder + capture transcript of Zoom for follow-up (consent required)
- Tag each measurement with test-id and timestamp (format: YYYYMMDD-<customer>-t1)

Decision criteria (help customer decide quickly):
- Go hosted if: latency p95 < target AND data residency allows egress OR approved VPC egress is fast to provision.
- Go dedicated if: cost per token at QPS target is lower AND you need reserved throughput for SLA.
- Go private if: policy/regulatory or air-gapped requirement exists and the customer accepts multi-week lead time and host ops burden.

Common obstacles & mitigation scripts (phrases to use):
- Obstacle: "We can't open ports to external services" => Script: "Can we trial with outbound-only egress to a set of fixed IPs; we can provide a short-lived allowlist and rotate after test?"
- Obstacle: "We need HSM integration" => Script: "We can scope an initial PoC using customer-managed KMS for key wrap; full HSM/PKCS#11 integration is a second-phase deliverable."

Follow-up deliverables (what Redwood will produce within 3 business days):
- One-page lab summary with measurements and recommended path (PDF)
- Action item list (owners + due dates) in a shared Google Sheet
- Risk register exported CSV
- Optional: trimmed recording clip of the test runs and measurement logs (if customer approves)

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Need to prepare a minimal harness that supports both hosted and dedicated endpoints automatically (script parameterized by URL + key).
- Confirm whether we can provide a small GPU trial VM for private test runs (ops approval).
- Put together quick cheat-sheet for customers on required firewall rules and egress IPs.

Appendix: quick-run test commands (for facilitator)
- happy path: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' -d '{"input":"<SAMPLE>"}' 
- long-context: python run_long_sequence.py --endpoint <URL> --key <KEY> --tokens 2048 --iterations 5
- capture util: sudo tcpdump -w capture.pcap host <redwood-ip> and tar/gzip after test

Scribe template (copy into Google Sheet):
- test-id, timestamp, test-type, endpoint, p50(ms), p95(ms), tokens, errors, cpu(%), gpu(%), egress_bytes, notes

Quick checklist for facilitator before session:
- Confirm attendee emails & Slack channel created
- Verify prework artifacts received
- Provision measurement VM or confirm host access
- Share slide deck + script with customer 24 hours before

End of draft.

Notes: Keep this file lightweight — it's intended to be copied into a session-specific doc where we swap in customer name, dates, and measurements. This is intentionally practical and workshop-first; not a polished sales deck.
